## YEMEN, REPUBLIC OF — profile (page 237)

- **Header facts:** Region: Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan & Pakistan; income group: Low-income; lending category: IDA; data status: Data as reported (A); population: 41.8 million; GNI: 20,996; unit line: US$ million, unless otherwise indicated.
- **Total external debt stock, 2025:** 7,481, **+4.9% from 2024**.

- **Figure 1. Total external debt, 2015–25:** 7,296 in 2015 and 7,481 in 2025. The line falls after 2015, stays low and fairly flat around 2017–19 (≈), rises in 2020 (≈) to a clear peak in **2021** (≈), then declines through 2024 (≈) before rebounding in 2025.

- **Figure 2. External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations:**
  - **Total external debt:** 7,481
    - **Public & publicly guaranteed (PPG):** 6,882
    - **Short-term:** 599
  - **Public & publicly guaranteed — by creditor type:** 6,882
    - **Multilateral:** 3,541
    - **Bilateral:** 3,341
  - **Multilateral:** 3,541
    - World Bank-IDA: 1,009
    - IMF-SDR allocations: 957
    - Other multilateral: 1,574
  - **Bilateral:** 3,341
    - Saudi Arabia: 1,306
    - Russian Federation: 1,203
    - Other bilateral: 833

- **Figure 3. Debt ratios, 2015–25:**
  - **External debt / exports:** 676%, **+3.4%**. Trend: rises early, no data shown for 2017–20, then resumes at a high level and edges up by 2025.
  - **External debt / GNI:** 34%, **+21.8%**. Trend: gradual increase from 2015 to 2018; no data shown after 2018.
  - **Debt service / exports:** 11%, **-13.7%**. Trend: declines early, no data shown for 2017–20, then rises sharply and eases slightly by 2025.
  - **Debt service / GNI:** 1%, **+39.8%**. Trend: low and broadly flat to slightly declining from 2015 to 2018; no data shown after 2018.

- **Figure 4. Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025:**
  - **Official creditors:** Maturity 4 yrs; Grace period 2 yrs; Interest rate 3.7%.
  - **Private creditors:** Maturity ..; Grace period ..; Interest rate ...

- **Notes:**
  - Note: Figure 3 shows no data values for the exports-based ratios in 2017–20, or for the GNI-based ratios after 2018.
  - Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025.

- **Source:** World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
